schema_note: count_unit (farm_count only): businesses (업체/개소) or producers (생산자수, persons). Each record: region_ko, region_en, province, year, metric (farm_count|area_ha|production_t), value, source_id, level (national|province|county|township|site). Extra fields: basis (total = licensed incl. idle; operating = producing; unspecified = source does not say), geo_key (KOSTAT 2018 si/gun code, or P35/P36/KR), note, corroborated_by, secondary (true = news source).

events.label: First solar salt pan in Sinan (Bigeum)
events.detail: Test pan begun March 1946 in Surim village, Bigeum; solar salt farms spread in Sinan from 1947.

events.label: National self-sufficiency
events.detail: National salt-pan area reached 10,500 ha and output 350,000 t, the first year of self-sufficiency.

events.label: Monopoly ends
events.detail: The Salt Monopoly Act was repealed on 30 Dec 1961; salt making was fully privatised from 1 Jan 1962.

events.label: Import liberalisation; closure subsidies
events.detail: Salt imports fully liberalised from 1 July 1997 (S05). Closure (폐전) support ran 1997-2004 per S06; S08 dates the period 1997-2005.

events.label: Lowest output
events.detail: National output fell to 155,951 t, the lowest recorded, the year before closure support ended.

events.label: Reclassified as food
events.detail: From March 2008 solar salt was reclassified from a mineral to a food under the amended Salt Management Act.

events.label: 54-day monsoon; solar-panel conversion
events.detail: Output fell in 2020 after a 54-day monsoon (S09, secondary). S06 cites more rain days, conversion of salt farms to solar power and an ageing workforce in the 2020s.

events.label: Jeonbuk: imports and land conversion
events.detail: Jeonbuk farms fell from 10 (1999) to 3 (2001); cheap Chinese salt and conversion of salt-farm land, including an F1 Grand Prix site, are cited.

events.label: Gomso salt farm halved
events.detail: Half of the Gomso salt farm (446,281 m²) was converted to fish farms and other uses when a salt-price collapse was expected.
